parts.title: What Are the 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die?
parts.subtitle: Written by a former New York Times restaurant critic, this substantial book will keep your appetite satisfied for a lifetime.
parts.article:
What Are the 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die

(A) When was the last time you sat down to a meal of harnam meshwi, also known as grilled pigeon, which is most likely to be found on a menu in Egypt? Or travelled to Oslo, Norway, for a breakfast of freshly caught shrimp? The answer is probably never.

(B) However, thanks to former New York Times restaurant critic, Smithsonian contributor and author Mimi Sheraton’s latest book, 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die, your culinary life is about to become much more interesting.

(C) Inspired by Patricia Schultz’s bestselling 1,000 Places to See Before You Die, which was also published by Workman Publishing, Sheraton has assembled 1,000 must-try dishes, restaurants, markets, cultural feasts and even some relatively universal foods, such as bananas, olive oil and whipped cream, which transcend regional categorisation.

(D) Selected from cuisines around the world, the items have been brought together in one large volume. The book also provides details about their historical and cultural contexts, advice on how to prepare particular dishes or where to try them, and several dozen recipes.

(E) The project took ten years to complete. It is both an impressive demonstration of Sheraton’s extensive knowledge of food -- she has been writing about the subject for sixty years -- and a celebration of the extraordinary diversity of the world’s cuisines.

(F) The book is the ultimate gift for a food lover. In the same way that 1,000 Places to See Before You Die reinvented the travel book, 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die is a joyful, informative, dazzling and mouth-watering life list of the finest food in the world.

(G) The book is organised not according to country or type of food, but according to the experience of eating itself. Its sections guide readers through categories such as "Street Food & Snacks", "Comfort Food" and "Sweets & Treats".

(H) This structure encourages unexpected discoveries. A reader searching for a classic French pastry might encounter a traditional Indonesian dessert and become fascinated by it.

(I) Sheraton’s entries are more than simple items in a list; they are miniature stories. She explains why a particular cheese from a remote Greek village is worth finding or how a particular noodle dish reflects the history of trade routes in Southeast Asia.

(J) This narrative approach transforms the book from a simple checklist into a compelling exploration of culture, history and human connections through food.

(K) Of course, a list containing 1,000 items is certain to provoke some controversy. Some critics question the inclusion of widely available foods such as bananas, arguing that this reduces the exclusivity of the list.

(L) Others have suggested that the book may be biased towards European and North American cuisines. Sheraton, however, defends her choices by referring to the extensive research and personal travels that informed them.

(M) She emphasises that the book is a personal but expert guide rather than a definitive and objective ranking. Its purpose, she states, is to inspire curiosity and appreciation, not to bring an end to debate.

(N) Ultimately, 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die serves as a passport to gastronomic adventure. It challenges readers to look beyond their culinary comfort zones, whether this involves searching for a rare ingredient, attempting a complicated recipe at home or simply ordering an unfamiliar dish at a local restaurant.

(O) For Sheraton, the book represents the culmination of a lifetime’s passion for food. It is an invitation to enjoy the remarkable diversity of flavours that the world has to offer, one unforgettable bite at a time.

questions.question: Mimi Sheraton is currently working as a restaurant critic for the New York Times.

analyses.content: 原文明确指出她是一名前任（former）《纽约时报》餐厅评论员，而不是像题目所说的那样现在正在（currently）做这份工作。
你可能会因为看到“New York Times���就激动地选了TRUE或NOT GIVEN，但千万别漏看了“former（前任）”这个决定性的时间词。

However, thanks to former New York Times restaurant critic, Smithsonian contributor and author Mimi Sheraton’s latest book, 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die, your culinary life is about to become much more interesting.

questions.question: The book 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die was directly inspired by a popular travel guide.

analyses.content: 原文提到这本书是受了畅销书《死前必去的1000个地方》的启发（Inspired by...），这正是一本备受欢迎的旅游指南（travel guide）。
你可能会觉得原文没直接出现“travel guide”这个词而不敢选TRUE，但《死前必去的1000个地方》本身就是一本典型的旅游书，完全符合题意。

Inspired by Patricia Schultz’s bestselling 1,000 Places to See Before You Die, which was also published by Workman Publishing, Sheraton has assembled 1,000 must-try dishes, restaurants, markets, cultural feasts and even some relatively universal foods, such as bananas, olive oil and whipped cream, which transcend regional categorisation.

questions.question: Sheraton’s book contains a recipe for every one of the 1,000 foods mentioned.

analyses.content: 题目说书里对这1000种食物“每一种（every one）”都提供了菜谱，但原文说书里只包含了“几十个（several dozen）”菜谱，数量完全对不上。
看到原文有“recipes（菜谱）”这个词你可能想当然地选TRUE，但一定要小心题目里“every one”这种极其绝对化的陷阱。

Selected from cuisines around the world, the items have been brought together in one large volume. The book also provides details about their historical and cultural contexts, advice on how to prepare particular dishes or where to try them, and several dozen recipes.

questions.question: The contents of the book are organised according to the geographical origins of the foods.

analyses.content: 原文直接否定了按地理位置分类的说法，明确写出这本书不是根据国家（not according to country）来组织的，而是根据吃东西的体验本身来组织的。
你可能会在其他段落看到许多不同国家的名字从而产生误解，但只要看准了这句“not according to country”，就能立刻锁定FALSE。

The book is organised not according to country or type of food, but according to the experience of eating itself. Its sections guide readers through categories such as "Street Food & Snacks", "Comfort Food" and "Sweets & Treats".

questions.question: Sheraton has been writing about food for sixty years.

analyses.content: 原文在破折号里清楚地写着，关于食物这个主题，她已经写了60年（she has been writing about the subject for sixty years），跟题目表述完全一致。
只要定位到明显的数字“sixty years”，直接对比主语和动作，这就是一道不需要多想的送分题。

The project took ten years to complete. It is both an impressive demonstration of Sheraton’s extensive knowledge of food -- she has been writing about the subject for sixty years -- and a celebration of the extraordinary diversity of the world’s cuisines.

analyses.content: 原文提到了菜品的历史背景（选项A对应historical and cultural contexts）、去哪找食物的建议（选项B对应where to try them）以及少量菜谱（选项D对应several dozen recipes），唯独没提过任何关于营养价值（nutritional information）的内容。
做这种EXCEPT（除了）的题，你只需要在原文里把提到过的A、B、D三个已知选项划掉，剩下的C自然就是原文没写的。

She emphasises that the book is a personal but expert guide rather than a definitive and objective ranking. Its purpose, she states, is to inspire curiosity and appreciation, not to bring an end to debate.

groups.contentHtml:
Mimi Sheraton’s Guide to the World’s Food
Mimi Sheraton’s book has been described as the for anyone who loves food. It is notable for its narrative approach, with the individual entries being presented as that explain the historical or cultural importance of particular dishes.
Although the book has attracted some because of the inclusion of widely available foods, Sheraton defends her choices by referring to her extensive and personal travels.
The ultimate purpose of the book is to encourage readers to move beyond their culinary and begin their own gastronomic adventures.

analyses.content: 顺着题目找“for anyone who loves food（给热爱食物的人）”，原文里正好有一模一样的对应句“for a food lover”，它前面的名词短语“ultimate gift”就是你要填的答案。
只要你锁定“food lover”这个强定位词，就能精准拔出这个词组，不用担心填偏。
The book is the ultimate gift for a food lover.
题目问每个条目是作为什么呈现的，原文明确说“它们是微型故事（they are miniature stories）”，紧接着的句子也解释了它们包含的历史和文化重要性。
你可能会只看前半句填“simple items”，但原文写的是“不仅仅是简单的列表条目（more than simple items）”，不要被否定意味的结构骗了。

Sheraton’s entries are more than simple items in a list; they are miniature stories. She explains why a particular cheese from a remote Greek village is worth finding or how a particular noodle dish reflects the history of trade routes in Southeast Asia.
题目说因为包含了随处可见的食物而引发了什么，原文明确说这样的列表肯定会激起一些“争议（provoke some controversy）”。
你可能会顺着意思填成下一句的“critics（批评家）”，但题目需要填的是被引发的事情（名词），而不是发起动作的人。

Of course, a list containing 1,000 items is certain to provoke some controversy. Some critics question the inclusion of widely available foods such as bananas, arguing that this reduces the exclusivity of the list.
题目说她通过提及广泛的什么和个人旅行来为自己辩护，原文原话就是“extensive research and personal travels”，直接照抄“research”即可填补空缺。
只要你找到了定位词“defends（辩护）”和“personal travels”，夹在中间的这个词绝对不会填错。
Sheraton, however, defends her choices by referring to the extensive research and personal travels that informed them.
题目说最终目的是鼓励读者超越他们的什么（move beyond），原文里的原话是“挑战读者超越他们的烹饪舒适区（look beyond their culinary comfort zones）”。
这道题需要你把“move beyond”和“look beyond”对应起来，注意字数要求是“NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS（不超过两个词）”，千万不要把题干里已经有的culinary也填进去了。

Ultimately, 1,000 Foods to Eat Before You Die serves as a passport to gastronomic adventure. It challenges readers to look beyond their culinary comfort zones, whether this involves searching for a rare ingredient, attempting a complicated recipe at home or simply ordering an unfamiliar dish at a local restaurant.
